Home
This page is currently awaiting content
A strong start. A considered choice. A future shaped with care.
Established in 1705, The Queen Anne upholds a proud tradition of inspiring generations of young people to thrive with confidence, character and purpose. Guided by our vision of Enjoy, Include, Achieve, children arrive each day into a community where they are known, supported and encouraged to aim high. Academic ambition sits comfortably alongside a warm, nurturing environment where every child is valued as an individual, building on a legacy of care, opportunity and achievement that spans more than three centuries.
Set beside the Long Walk, The Queen Anne offers a rare combination: the nurturing atmosphere of a village school and the exceptional opportunities afforded by its town location. As a Church of England school, we enjoy close links with All Saints' Church, fostering a strong sense of community, shared values and belonging.
Our small school with a high adult-to-pupil ratio, ensures that learning is supportive and appropriately challenging. High expectations encourage pupils to think deeply, learn confidently and take pride in their work.
Our broad and ambitious curriculum is brought to life through our rich co-curricular opportunities and a strong focus on creativity, communication and problem-solving.
Here at The Queen Anne, learning does not stay in the classroom. Step outside, and explore our Little Woods, Potager, Forest Garden, ancient woodland, Lost Garden and pond; spaces where curiosity leads to discovery and learning feels real.
Families choose The Queen Anne for its strong foundations, inclusive community and inspiring setting. Whether you are part of our local community or commute from further afield, your child will be welcomed into a school where they are known, valued and encouraged to thrive.
Visit usWe would be delighted to welcome you and show you The Queen Anne in action.

pageCache.pageTitle: The Queen Anne Royal Free C.E. First School - British Values
pageCache.text:
British Values
At The Queen Anne Royal Free, British Values are not taught in isolation but lived daily through how children speak, listen, learn and grow together. Rooted in our Christian ethos, they are brought to life through the Fruit of the Spirit, shaping both character and culture.
Pupils learn that every voice matters, developing an understanding of democracy through discussion, collaboration and shared decision-making. They come to see that rules create a safe and respectful environment, building their understanding of the rule of law alongside growing self-control and responsibility.
Children are encouraged to take ownership of their learning, experiencing individual liberty within a nurturing setting that builds confidence and independence. Relationships are central to school life, with mutual respect modelled and expected in all interactions.
Our diverse community fosters appreciation of different faiths, cultures and beliefs, nurturing understanding, empathy and belonging. Together, British Values and the fruit of the Spirit shape pupils who are thoughtful, respectful and compassionate, ready to contribute positively to the world around them.
Our Curriculum

pageCache.pageTitle: The Queen Anne Royal Free C.E. First School - Outdoor Learning
pageCache.text:
Outdoor Learning
At The Queen Anne First School, the natural world is not simply a backdrop to education; it is an integral part of it. Set within beautiful grounds, including pockets of ancient woodland, a wildlife pond, rare tree species and a rich variety of habitats, our outdoor spaces provide an exceptional environment in which children can explore, discover and thrive.
Every outdoor space is thoughtfully used to enrich learning across the curriculum, bringing learning to life through first-hand experiences and enquiry. Our grounds are also a thriving sanctuary for wildlife. Children might spot a family of pheasants on a morning walk, search for stag beetles beneath fallen logs or observe newts and bats in their natural habitats. These moments of discovery nurture curiosity, confidence and a deep sense of connection to the environment.
Our commitment to sustainability and environmental learning has received prestigious recognition. Through Citizen Science projects, participation in Education Nature Park and our involvement in the Royal Windsor Horticultural Society's Nature Studies Pilot, our pupils become young scientists and thoughtful custodians of the natural world.
This dedication has been recognised with the prestigious Dorothy Morley Silver Award for environmental achievement in 2024 and a Silver Award at the Windsor Flower Show for our wheelbarrow, on the theme of Rooted in Nature.
Here children do not simply learn about nature; they learn within it, from it and alongside it.
Come and see our young explorers in action! Our children loved exploring All Saints church grounds, using their mapping skills to investigate the trees, wildlife, plants, and natural habitats all around them. Click the video below to join them on their exciting outdoor adventure and see their learning come to life!

pageCache.pageTitle: The Queen Anne Royal Free C.E. First School - Assessment
pageCache.text:
Assessment
How do we assess pupils’ learning at The Queen Anne ?
We gather a range of formative and summative evidence throughout the year to monitor progress and attainment.
Formative assessment (Assessment for Learning) gives information on how well a child is progressing to meet a given objective or target and provides information to assist the next steps. High-quality first teaching ensures that ongoing assessment for learning is an integral part of the daily classroom context for all pupils. Teachers continually make assessments of children’s progress both during and after lessons. The ongoing assessments are used to support children’s progress. Progress is assessed using a wide range of evidence including questioning, discussion, analysis of work , written and oral feedback, observations, self-reflection and peer reflection.
Summative assessment (Assessment of Learning) gives information on how well an objective has been achieved at the end of a period of time. Achievement is reviewed at the end of each term through work scrutiny, specific tests & checks and teacher judgement.
ASSESSMENT IN THE FOUNDATION STAGE
The Foundation Stage: the children participate in the Reception Baseline Assessment (RBA) within the first 6 weeks of starting in the foundation stage class at The Queen Anne.
RECEPTION BASELINE INFORMATION FOR PARENTS
Statutory Framework for the Early Years’ Foundation Stage
Towards the end of the Summer term, the E.Y.F.S. Profile is completed. The E.Y.F.S. Profile provides parents and carers, practitioners and teachers with a well-rounded picture of a child’s knowledge, understanding and abilities, their attainment against expected levels, and their readiness for Year 1. The Profile reflects practitioners’ own knowledge and professional judgement of a child to inform discussions with parents and carers, and any other adults whom the teacher, parent or carer judges can offer a useful contribution.
Each child’s level of development must be assessed against the early learning goals. Teachers must indicate whether children are meeting expected levels of development, or if they are not yet reaching expected levels(‘emerging’).
STATUTORY ASSESSMENTS IN KEY STAGE 1
At the end of Year 1, the children participate in the Phonic Screening Check.
Phonics Screening Check Information for Parents PDF
STATUTORY ASSESSMENT IN YEAR 4
Towards the end of Year 4 , the children participate in the statutory Multiplication Tables Check
At the end of the summer term, teachers use their professional judgement to determine if the children in Year 1-Year 4 are working at expected age -related expectations with judgements of ‘below’, ‘at expected’ or ‘greater depth’.

pageCache.pageTitle: The Queen Anne Royal Free C.E. First School - Co-curricular Opportunities
pageCache.text:
Co-curricular Opportunities
Our co-curricular programme is an integral part of an enriched education. It is carefully designed to extend learning beyond the classroom for all, providing pupils with experiences that broaden horizons, deepen understanding and cultivate confidence, curiosity and character. Through a rich blend of educational visits, leadership opportunities, expert teaching and cultural experiences, pupils develop the knowledge and dispositions needed to thrive. These moments, big and small, enrich our curriculum and bring learning to life for our children.
Co-curricular Opportunities 25-26
Enriching Local History
A distinctive feature of our provision is our structured, progressive programme of study linked to Windsor Castle, ensuring that each year group builds knowledge and understanding over time through carefully sequenced experiences.
Reception pupils began their journey with a river voyage along the Thames, gaining their first perspective of Windsor Castle from the water and developing early observational and language skills through rich first-hand experience.
Year 1 pupils explored Windsor Castle as a royal residence, developing their understanding of monarchy and the role of the King through immersive, age-appropriate learning.
Year 2 pupils engaged in historical enquiry, comparing the Great Fire of London with the fire at Windsor Castle, developing early disciplinary thinking around cause, consequence and historical significance.
Year 3 pupils visited St George’s Chapel, deepening their understanding of its architectural, religious and national importance within British heritage.
Year 4 pupils participated in a bespoke study session exploring Windsor Castle’s significance at local, national and global levels, synthesising prior learning and engaging in more abstract historical thinking.
Across all year groups, these experiences ensured that pupils encounter history not as isolated facts, but as a living narrative rooted in place and identity.
Outdoor Learning & Environmental Stewardship
Outdoor learning is a defining strength of our co-curricular offer, fostering curiosity, resilience and a deep respect for the natural world.
We are proud to be a pilot school for the Royal Windsor Flower Show Nature Studies programme, delivered in partnership with Little Muddy Boots. Through weekly outdoor sessions, pupils engaged in planting, growing and observing seasonal change, developing scientific understanding and environmental stewardship through sustained hands-on learning.
This commitment to environmental education was further enriched through:
Personal Development
Pupil leadership was embedded throughout school life, providing authentic opportunities for responsibility, voice and influence.
Our Wellbeing Champions led assemblies and represented the school at local emotional wellbeing conferences, contributing thoughtfully to wider conversations around mental health and wellbeing in education.
In partnership with the local Police Community Support Officer (PCSO), pupils took part in carefully tailored safeguarding and personal development sessions. These include:
In addition, pupils in Years 3 and 4 undertook Bikeability training, developing confidence, independence and essential road safety awareness.
Cultural Opportunities
Our co-curricular programme nurtures creativity, expression and a lifelong love of learning.
Pupils benefit from a termly Book Burst session led by a specialist in children’s literature, who curates engaging, high-quality texts designed to inspire reading for pleasure and broaden literary horizons. Visiting authors further enrich this provision through workshops that illuminate the craft of writing and encourage pupils’ own creative voice.
In the arts, pupils worked with a specialist art practitioner, in Year 2, where they developed and refined their sketchbook skills and a sophisticated understanding of line, shape, tone and form. All teachers developed their sketchbook skills through training.
Musical development was supported through specialist vocal tuition, with pupils performing confidently in both school and community settings. Our Year 3 & Year 4 pupils performed at Windsor Parish Church, strengthening technique, expression and stage presence.
Cultural enrichment was further enhanced through our annual theatre visit. This year our younger children enjoyed a high-quality live performance of The Comet which supported their imaginative storytelling and writing.
Pupils were given regular opportunities to take part in a range of performances, present and reflect on their learning. End-of-year assemblies for Years 1–3 provided a platform to share progress and celebrate achievement with families, while Year 4 culminated their primary journey with a full-scale production demonstrating confidence, creativity and teamwork.
A group of Year 3 pupils took part in a film project produced by Notice Films, developing their creativity, communication skills and confidence. Their work will be showcased at the Windsor Film Festival in September 2027.
Sport, Challenge & Physical Development
Through the Windsor Schools Sports Partnership, pupils access a broad and inclusive programme of sporting festivals and competitions, including benchball tournaments, skipping events and leadership development opportunities. These experiences foster teamwork, resilience and a commitment to personal excellence.
Complementary enrichment includes first aid workshops delivered by the University of Reading, where pupils develop practical life skills through hands-on, memorable learning experiences.
A residential visit for Year 4 to an outdoor adventure centre further develops independence, resilience and collaborative skills through shared challenge and experiential learning.
Science
Our co-curricular programme provides rich opportunities for pupils to explore science through hands-on, real-world experiences.
Foundation Stage pupils developed their early scientific curiosity through direct interaction with farm animals, building an understanding of living things, habitats and care for animals in a meaningful, experiential context.
Year 1 and Year 2 pupils extended this learning through visits to Bocket’s Farm, where they observed animals, explored food production and deepened their understanding of life cycles, seasonal change and the natural environment.
Across the school, scientific thinking was further enriched through an engaging forensic science workshop, where pupils investigated evidence, solved problems and applied logical reasoning in practical, hands-on scenarios.
In addition, pupils experienced memorable encounters with animals and seasonal learning through special visits such as reindeer visiting the school, which provided opportunities for observation, questioning and discussion linked to living things and the natural world.

pageCache.pageTitle: The Queen Anne Royal Free C.E. First School - Foundation Stage: Reception Class
pageCache.text:
Foundation Stage: Reception Class
Intent Our Reception curriculum is designed to ignite a lifelong love of learning by providing children with a rich, stimulating, and nurturing start to their educational journey. Rooted in the Early Years Foundation Stage, it aims to develop confident, curious, and articulate learners who are eager to explore the world around them. We place a strong emphasis on communication, early literacy and numeracy, and personal development, while also fostering creativity, independence, resilience, and a sense of wonder.
Implementation Learning is delivered through an inspiring blend of purposeful play and carefully structured adult-led experiences. Children learn within a thoughtfully designed environment that includes engaging provision areas such as imaginative role-play, construction challenges, creative arts, early writing stations, reading corners filled with high-quality texts, and a vibrant outdoor learning space.
Phonics is taught daily in focused, lively sessions that build strong foundations for reading and writing. Stories, songs, and rich language experiences are woven throughout the day to expand vocabulary and comprehension. Mathematical understanding is developed through practical exploration including counting, problem-solving, and investigating patterns and shapes in meaningful contexts.
Adults extend thinking through questioning, modelling, and targeted interaction. They observe closely to ensure each child is supported and challenged appropriately. Personal, social, and emotional development is embedded across all activities, with children encouraged to collaborate, communicate, take risks, and develop independence.
Impact Children leave Reception as confident, enthusiastic learners who are well-prepared for the demands of Year 1 and beyond. They demonstrate strong early reading and writing skills, a secure foundation in number and mathematical thinking, and a growing ability to articulate ideas clearly and creatively.
They show curiosity, resilience, and independence in their approach to learning, alongside excellent social skills and emotional awareness. Most importantly, they develop a genuine excitement for discovery and a belief in their own potential, providing the foundations for an ambitious and successful educational journey.
Our Curriculum

pageCache.pageTitle: The Queen Anne Royal Free C.E. First School - Pupil Leadership
pageCache.text:
Pupil Leadership
Leadership at The Queen Anne is not reserved for a few; it is something every child is encouraged to experience in meaningful, age-appropriate ways throughout their time with us.
Across all year groups, pupils are trusted with real responsibility. Children take on roles such as Emotional Wellbeing Leads, supporting their peers and helping to promote a positive school culture. Sports leaders encourage participation, teamwork and fair play, both in lessons and at events.
Leadership is also woven into everyday classroom life. Children take on small but important responsibilities, such as classroom monitors, learning partners and helping to organise resources. These daily roles build independence, confidence and accountability from the earliest years.
Pupils also represent the school in a wide range of contexts, including sporting fixtures, festivals and competitions, as well as leading on ecology, singing and other whole-school initiatives. These experiences help children develop confidence, communication skills and pride in representing their school.
Leadership is visible at many moments across the school day: supporting a peer, leading a group activity, speaking confidently, or representing the school in the wider community.
Leadership is learnt through experience. By offering opportunities at every level, we ensure all pupils develop their voice, take responsibility and grow as confident, capable young leaders.

pageCache.pageTitle: The Queen Anne Royal Free C.E. First School - Wraparound Care
pageCache.text:
Wraparound Care
Exceptional wraparound care is provided at The Queen Anne Royal Free CE First School, offering a safe, welcoming and engaging environment for children beyond the school day. Our extended provision is based on site and led by familiar school staff.
Drop & Stop (Before School)
Drop & Stop from 8.00am and Meet & Greet from 8.20 a.m. provide a range of supervised activities with a healthy snack and drink. We offer a safe and calm start to the school day for all children.
Need a slightly earlier start to the day?
Take a look at Playball Active Start in our External Clubs section. Running on Wednesday and Thursday mornings from 7.30am to 8.40am, it's a fun, active way for children to begin the day with games, movement and exercise before heading into class, happy and ready to learn.
Stay & Play (After School)
Running from the end of the school day until 4.30pm or 6.00pm, Stay & Play provides a relaxed and enjoyable setting with a variety of activities. Children attending our external clubs on site are able to attend Stay & Play from 4.30 p.m. - 6 p.m. if desired.
We offer a range of paid clubs delivered by specialist external providers. Our current clubs can be viewed using the link in this section.
Holiday provision is available during selected school holidays, offering children the opportunity to take part in high-quality, engaging activities in a safe and familiar setting. This includes excellent outdoor learning activities that encourage exploration, independence and a love of the natural world.
Use the links in this section to find out more.

pageCache.pageTitle: The Queen Anne Royal Free C.E. First School - Remote Learning
pageCache.text:
Remote Learning
At The Queen Anne Royal Free, we use Tapestry to support high-quality communication and continuity of learning between school and home.
In the event of remote learning, Tapestry provides a clear and accessible platform where pupils can continue their learning journey with carefully planned activities, guidance and resources shared by teachers. Work is designed to reflect our in-school curriculum, ensuring continuity, structure and meaningful progression.
Tapestry also enables strong partnership with families, allowing parents to view learning, share achievements and communicate directly with teachers. Support via Tapestry ensures that children remain connected, supported and engaged, even when learning away from the classroom.
Our approach to remote learning reflects the same high expectations as our classroom provision, ensuring every child can continue to learn, develop and thrive wherever they are.
Remote Learning

pageCache.pageTitle: The Queen Anne Royal Free C.E. First School - Reporting To Parents & Carers
pageCache.text:
Reporting To Parents & Carers
How do we share information about the curriculum with parents?
Class meetings with the teacher take place at the start of each term. The teacher will discuss the curriculum for the term ahead and explain specific literacy and maths techniques.
Individual meetings with the class teacher take place in the Autumn and Summer term. We invite you to bring your child to these meetings to be part of the discussion about their learning. As our belief is there should be no surprises at parents evening, any concerns should have been raised either by parents or school before the individual meetings. We would like the meeting to be an opportunity to celebrate your child’s learning. Children of all ages benefit from talking about their work and ways to make it even better.
Written Reports
All children receive a short written report in the spring and summer terms. Parents are able to make an appointment with the teacher if they wish to discuss any aspect of the report.
Reporting To Parents & Carers

pageCache.pageTitle: The Queen Anne Royal Free C.E. First School - Sport Premium
pageCache.text:
Sport Premium
We place great importance on physical education, wellbeing and active participation in sport as part of a balanced and ambitious curriculum.
The Sport Premium funding is used strategically to enhance the quality and breadth of physical education, improve teaching and learning in PE, and ensure all pupils benefit from high-quality sporting experiences.
We invest in specialist coaching, staff development and enriched sporting opportunities that enable pupils to develop skill, confidence and enjoyment across a wide range of physical activities.
Our provision is designed to ensure that all children, regardless of ability, are actively engaged and appropriately challenged. We aim to develop physical competence alongside key personal qualities such as teamwork, resilience, discipline and respect.
Sport Premium funding also supports increased participation in competitive sport, both within school and through interschool events, ensuring pupils experience opportunities to represent the school and perform as part of a team.
We continually review the impact of this provision to ensure it leads to sustained improvements in teaching quality, pupil engagement and overall outcomes in physical education.
